statement: Each sheet of a book has an odd page on the front and the next page on the back, like 1 and 2. Tim tears out pages 5 to 12. How many sheets is that?

choices.misconception: I thought page 5 is on the back of page 4, so I counted sheets 4 and 5, 6 and 7, and so on up to 12 and 13.
I took 5 away from 12 instead of counting the sheets.
I counted the pages, not the sheets.
I thought each page was a whole sheet with two sides, so I doubled the 8 pages.

hints: Which page is on the back of page 5?
Every sheet starts with an odd page and ends with the next even page. Pair the pages up from 5 to 12, then count the pairs.
The sheets are 5 and 6, then 7 and 8, then 9 and 10, then 11 and 12.

solutions.reliable: Page 5 is odd, so it is on the front of a sheet with page 6 on the back. The pages pair up as 5 and 6, 7 and 8, 9 and 10, 11 and 12. That is 4 sheets. The idea to keep: odd and even numbers take turns, so a run that starts odd and ends even splits neatly into pairs.
solutions.elegant: There are 8 pages from 5 to 12, starting with an odd page and ending with an even one, so they fill whole sheets: 8 pages make 4 sheets.

whyOnTest: Odd and even numbers take turns, and pairing them correctly is the whole problem, while pairing an even page with the next odd one gives an extra sheet.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
